_purpose: Every number the paper cites lives here once, with the run and artifact it is re-derived from. tools/constants/check.py and audit.py enforce it; tools/constants/export.py writes the paper's macros from it.

_schema.value: the number (or list); null means not yet measured, and the note says why
_schema.card: the GPU the number is about, as the machine reported it; 'none' for a number about no card
_schema.context: the context length C the number was measured at; 'n/a' where it does not apply
_schema.timing_scope: one of _timing_scopes, or 'n/a' for a number that is not a time or a rate
_schema.run: measured only: the runs/<run-id> directory whose artifact the audit re-derives the value from
_schema.artifact: measured only: the file in that run directory
_schema.inputs: projected only: the constants keys the cost model read
_schema.note: one or two sentences; for external, the URL

_grades.measured: made by a driver in this repository; audit.py re-derives it from `artifact` in `run`
_grades.derived: arithmetic over other entries; check.py recomputes it from the entries it names
_grades.projected: the cost model, with the model's inputs named; never presented as a measurement
_grades.external: read from a public source, with its URL in the note
_grades.asserted: an assumption the owner made, with the reason in the note

_timing_scopes.commit: the commitment path only: interpolation, low-degree extension and Merkle hashing of the committed trees
_timing_scopes.stwo total: commit plus the prover's own call: constraint evaluation, quotients, out-of-domain sampling, FRI
_timing_scopes.whole wall: trace generation, interaction generation, stwo total and serialization, summed per segment; it does not include reading the witness or building the layer
_timing_scopes.loop: the one-process segment loop's own wall-clock time, which does include the witness read and the layer build; pipelined loops overlap one segment's generation with another's proving
_timing_scopes.primitive: one primitive of the proof system on its own (a hash, a field operation, a lookup, a fold), timed by the vendored library's benchmark harness; not a scope of any proof and not comparable with the four above

cost.h100_reference_usd_per_hour.note: RunPod published on-demand list price, Secure Cloud tier, H100 SXM 80 GB, https://www.runpod.io/gpu-models/h100-sxm (page updated 2026-08-27, retrieved 2026-08-31). Paired with the H200 rate from the same provider, tier and date.

cost.h200_reference_usd_per_hour.note: RunPod published on-demand list price, Secure Cloud tier, H200 141 GB, https://www.runpod.io/gpu-models/h200 (page updated 2026-08-27, retrieved 2026-08-31). The higher tier is the conservative choice for a cost claim.

hardware.h200.hbm_gbps_spec.note: NVIDIA H200 data sheet, HBM3e memory bandwidth, https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/h200/. A specification figure; this project never measured the card's own bandwidth.

deepprove.tpm_seq512_basefold.note: DeepProve, https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1112, Table 2, sequence length 512 with the BaseFold commitment: 512 tokens / 2.94 min. Their time counts proving only and excludes quantized inference and trace recording, which our whole-wall and loop scopes include; their attention depth is bounded by the sequence length.

verinf.maverick.positions.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: one forward pass over a 500-token prompt and a 500-token greedy continuation, all 1000 positions proved.

verinf.maverick.prover_hours.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: Llama-4-Maverick (400B parameters, 17B active), the 1000-position forward pass, prover peak 78.1 GB of GPU memory.

verinf.maverick.tok_s.note: verinf.maverick.positions / (verinf.maverick.prover_hours x 3600). Not a number they state; all 1000 positions are proved where our decode rows prove output tokens only.

verinf.maverick.proof_gb.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: 40 opened columns; proof size grows linearly with the witness at their fixed parameters.

verinf.maverick.verify_hours.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: verification on 20 CPU cores, peak 75.7 GB; interactive, per-challenge soundness about 2^-16.6.

verinf.maverick.bound_bits_per_token.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: the bound on unexplained information per token over the 500-token continuation. Their statement bounds information; it does not prove the exact computation or the token choice.

verinf.llama2_7b.prover_minutes.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: Llama-2-7B, 32 layers, real checkpoint weights, prover peak 11.2 GB, 1.44 GB proof at 10 opened columns.

verinf.gb10_measured_bandwidth_gbps.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, appendix A.5: the memory bandwidth their NTT is bound by, as they measured it, not the GB10's specification figure.

verinf.gb10_vs_h200_bandwidth_ratio.note: verinf.gb10_measured_bandwidth_gbps / hardware.h200.hbm_gbps_spec: their measured rate over an NVIDIA specification figure. Our commitment path is bound by hashing, not by memory bandwidth, so this compares hardware classes and nothing else.

cells.headline.c4096.fresh.note: Fresh committed cells over the sequence's 288 segments, added up from the run's 5 slice outputs; 78.171 M per proved position.

secs.headline.c4096.commit.note: The commitment path, added up over every segment of the sequence.

secs.headline.c4096.stwo_total.note: Commit plus the prover's own call, added up over every segment.

secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall.note: Trace generation, interaction generation, stwo total and serialization, added up per segment; it does not count reading the witness or building the segment, which is what the loop scope adds.

secs.headline.c4096.loop.note: The 5 segment-loop processes' own wall-clock time added up. It counts reading the witness and building the segment, and each segment's generation overlaps the previous one's proving, so it is neither a subset nor a superset of the whole-wall row.

segments.headline.c4096.note: 9 token blocks of 32 layer segments. The output head's segment is not among them: an honest head segment is refused at this prover commit (zk-prover #58), so the sequence is proved from the embedding up to the last layer's residual and the token the head emits is bound by nothing.

positions.headline.c4096.note: 4096 prompt positions and 512 output positions, every one of them proved from the embedding up through all 32 layers.

mem.headline.c4096.peak_mib.note: The most the card reported holding at any moment of the segment loop, sampled once a second. The card has 81,559 MiB.

pos_s.headline.c4096.whole_wall.note: positions.headline.c4096 / secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall. Positions and not tokens: the prompt is proved as well as the output (docs/decisions).

pos_s.headline.c4096.loop.note: positions.headline.c4096 / secs.headline.c4096.loop. Positions and not tokens: the prompt is proved as well as the output (docs/decisions).

segments.probe.c16384.note: The segments the two compared loops proved: layers 1 to 4 of the last token block, whose prefix is the whole 16,384-token prompt. They are the shape 1,023 of the headline plan's 1,056 segments have; layer 0's is the other one and is measured on its own.

cells.probe.c16384.fresh.note: Fresh committed cells over those four segments; 2.267 G each on average, against 1.251 G for the average segment of the context 4,096 sequence. The pipelined loop committed the same cells and produced the same four proof digests.

mem.probe.c16384.serial_peak_mib.note: The most the card reported holding at any moment of the loop with the pipeline off, sampled once a second. The card has 81,559 MiB. The prover's own high-water mark for the same loop is 75,894,751,232 bytes, which is this number to the MiB.

mem.probe.c16384.pipelined_peak_mib.note: The same four segments with the pipeline on, which holds two segments at once. It peaked at the same number as the loop that holds one, so at this context the second segment in flight cost the card nothing.

mem.probe.c16384.layer0_peak_mib.note: Layer 0 of the same block, proved on its own. Its statement carries the embedding gadget, which no other layer's does, and it is the largest segment of the headline plan: 6,464 MiB above the others and 2,716 MiB below the card.

secs.probe.c16384.serial_loop.note: The loop's own wall-clock time over four segments with the pipeline off: 57.18 s a segment, against 12.82 s at context 4,096 where the segments are a third of the size.

secs.probe.c16384.pipelined_loop.note: The same four segments with the pipeline on: 43.95 s a segment, 23.1 per cent less than the loop that holds one segment, for the same committed cells and the same four proof digests.

mem.probe.c16384.pipelined_l0_peak_mib.note: Layer 0 and layer 1 together under the pipeline, which is the pair the headline loop forms at the start of every block and the only pair that holds the plan's largest segment. It peaked at what layer 0 peaked at alone, so the second segment in flight cost the card nothing even here.

secs.probe.c16384.layer0_loop.note: Layer 0 of the last block, proved on its own with the pipeline off: one segment, and the slowest in the plan as well as the largest.

secs.probe.c16384.pipelined_l0_loop.note: Layers 0 and 1 under the pipeline: 75.31 s a segment against 94.67 s for layer 0 alone, so the pipeline helps on the pair that holds the largest segment too.

cells.microbench.compose_fresh.note: Fresh committed cells of the one synthetic segment this run proves, the prover's recorded sound shape with the five GKR reductions on. It is the denominator of the commitment rate below and nothing else; a segment this size is not a throughput row.

secs.microbench.compose_commit.note: The commitment path of that proof on the reference backend: interpolation, low-degree extension and Merkle hashing of the committed trees. Its low-degree test took 1.989 s of the same proof and its whole prove call 4.835 s.

rate.microbench.commit.note: Committed cells over the seconds the commitment path took, both from the same proof. This is the cost model's commitment-rate input, measured on the host's cores; a card's own rate is what a sequence run measures on real segments.

hash.merkle_simd_secs.note: A micro-benchmark of one primitive of the proof system, run by the vendored library's own benchmark on the host's cores with no card. It is a time but it is not a scope of a proof, which is why the scope is not one of the four: nothing here proves anything. One Merkle commitment over 16,777,216 field elements (65536 rows of 256 columns) with the Blake2s hasher on the packed backend.

hash.merkle_cpu_secs.note: A micro-benchmark of one primitive of the proof system, run by the vendored library's own benchmark on the host's cores with no card. The same commitment over the same elements on the unpacked backend, which is 82.2 times slower and is the reason the packed one exists.
